questions.question:
A statement is given followed by two arguments I and II. Read the statement and the arguments carefully and select the appropriate answer from the given options.

Statement:

Reclaimed land should be avoided as it only has disadvantages.

Arguments:

I. Many countries have no option but to reclaim land to provide for the increasing population.

II. Land that is reclaimed has long lasting effect on nature as it deteriorates ecosystems and biodiversity.

options.text: I weakens, while II strengthens the statement
II weakens, while I strengthens the statement
Both I and II strengthen the statement
Both I and II weaken the statement

questions.solution:
__Statement__:

Reclaimed land should be avoided as it only has disadvantages.

__Arguments__:

I. Many countries have no option but to reclaim land to provide for the increasing population → In this argument, there is an advantage shared about the reclaimed land but the statement suggests that it has only disadvantages since both of them points are against each other, the argument weakens the statement.

II. Land that is reclaimed has a long-lasting effect on nature as it deteriorates ecosystems and biodiversity → Here the bad effects of reclaimed land are discussed which in turn favours the point indicated in the statement so both of them lead towards the same direction i.e., negative effects of reclaimed lands, therefore, the argument strengthens the statement.

So the argument I weaken the statement, while argument II strengthens the statement.

Hence the correct answer is **"****I weakens, while II strengthens the statement".**

questions.question: Let r be the greatest number which when divides 41, 71 and 91 leaves the same remainder. Find the LCM of r and 45.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divisor r leaving the same remainder = HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

r = HCF of |71 − 41|, |91 − 71|, and |91 − 41|

r = HCF(30, 20, 50) = 10

Required LCM = LCM of 10 and 45 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three numbers: 41, 71, and 91

Second number to find LCM with r: 45

**Concept Used:**

The greatest number r that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder is the HCF of their absolute differences.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Differences = |71 − 41|, |91 − 71|, and |91 − 41|

⇒ Differences = 30, 20, and 50

⇒ Now, we find the HCF of 30, 20, and 50 to get r.

⇒ 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ 50 = 2 × 5²

⇒ Common prime factors are 2 and 5.

⇒ r = HCF(30, 20, 50) = 2 × 5 = 10

⇒ We need to find the LCM of r (which is 10) and 45.

⇒ 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ 45 = 3² × 5

⇒ LCM(10, 45) = 2 × 3² × 5

⇒ LCM = 2 × 9 × 5 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

**__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that perfectly divides two or more numbers. It is obtained by multiplying the lowest powers of all common prime factors.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest number which is perfectly divisible by two or more given numbers. It is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved.

Property of Remainder Divisors

When asked to find the greatest number dividing x, y, and z to leave the same remainder, the required number is always the HCF of the absolute differences |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

options.text: The boiling points increase with decreasing molecular mass.

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Homologous Series__**

 __
 
• ​Any homologous sequence exhibits a gradation in physical attributes as the** molecule mass rises.**
 
• This is due to the fact that when **molecule mass increases, melting and boiling points also rise**.
 
• Similar gradations can be seen in other physical attributes like **solubility in a particular solvent.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Because only **immediate dipole-induced dipole** interactions can contribute to the intermolecular forces, **alkanes have relatively low boiling points**.
 
• Because of the **carbon-chlorine polar link (+C-Cl-),** which creates a permanent dipole and adds a tiny amount to the intermolecular forces, **primary halogenoalkanes (n-alkyl halides) have somewhat higher boiling temperatures than alkanes.**
 
• Because the** N-H bond (-N-H+) **is more polar than the C-Cl bond and this permanent dipole** - permanent dipol**e interactions will result in hydrogen bonding, but not to the same extent as for alcohols, primary aliphatic amines are the** second highest boiling compounds.**
 
• **Aldehydes and isomeric ketones **are both primary aliphatic amines that are linear in structure. It would seem that the hydrogen bonding in the amines has roughly the same impact here as the permanent dipole - permanent dipole intermolecular attractive interactions caused by the polarised **carbonyl bond (+C=O-)**.
 
• 
 
Due to the additional** intermolecular tension of hydrogen bonds, alcohols (alkanols) exhibit much higher boiling temperatures than alkanes, BUT ONLY for the lower members.**

 
 
• 
 
Because there are additional >C=O... >C=0 attractions in addition to hydrogen bonding, or you could argue that there are two sites on the molecule for hydrogen bonding, again only for the lower members of the series, and dimers are easily formed for the lower members of the series, **carboxylic acids (also known as alkanoic acids) are even higher than alcohols.**

__

 __
 
• The gills in fish are used to assist with **breathing**. The majority of fish have **gills on each side of their heads**.
 
• A huge surface area for gas exchange is provided by the tissues known as gills, which are composed of** feathery structures known as gill filaments.** Aquatic organisms need a lot of surface area for gas exchange because the water's dissolved oxygen content is so low.
 
• The rows of fish gill filaments are arranged in the **gill arch**. Lamellae, which are discs dotted with capillaries, make up each filament.
 
• Through these tiny blood arteries, blood enters and exits the gills. Even though fish's gills only cover a small portion of their bodies, the large respiratory surface that filaments create gives the entire creature **effective gas exchange.**
 
• Fish use their** mouths to pump oxygen-rich water over their gills**. The blood inside the capillary network absorbs the dissolved oxygen as water flows over the gill filaments.
 
• The circulatory system then transports carbon dioxide from the body, which is expelled by the gills, and distributes oxygen to all body tissues before reaching the cells. Once the water has passed the gills, it leaves the fish's body through openings on the sides of the throat or through the **operculum, a** **flap that is typically found in bony fish and covers and shields the gills.**
 
• 
 
Several fish have several **gill openings, including sharks and lampreys. Bony fish called rohu only has one gill opening on either side.**

 **Pectoral fin**: A fish's pectoral fin is typically seen exactly next to its gills. Fish use these tiny, arm-like appendages to turn and steer in the water. Moreover, they manage depth.
 
 

 **Position 4(Pelvic Fin or Anal Fin)**
 The** pelvic fin,** often referred to as the ventral fin, is located near the base of a fish's body. This fin, which serves as both a brake and a propeller, is crucial for the majority of complex movements. Pelvic fins can also be utilised to hover and "ground walk" over objects. **Anal fin**: Anal fins are normally situated in the middle of the body, halfway between the** pelvic and tail fins**. In order to maintain their erect posture, narrow or laterally compressed fish typically have longer anal fins.

• The term "**atomic radius**" refers to the distance that separates an atom's outermost shell from its center in the** nucleus.**

• Atomic size** decreases** over time as **nuclear charge increases** while the number of shells stays the same.
 
• Because of this, electrons are pulled toward the nucleus from the outermost shell, **reducing its size**.

questions.question: If a + (1)/(a) = 9 , then the value of a³ + (1)/(a³) is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k

Given a + 1/a = 9, so here k = 9.

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 9³ − 3 × 9

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 729 − 27 = 702

**∴ The correct answer is 702.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + 1/a = 9

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cubing both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (a + 1/a)³ = 9³

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ + 3 × a × (1/a) × (a + 1/a) = 729

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ + 3 × 1 × (a + 1/a) = 729

⇒ Substituting the value of (a + 1/a) = 9:

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ + 3 × 9 = 729

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ + 27 = 729

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 729 − 27

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 702

**∴ The correct answer is 702.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Algebraic Identity

Minus to Plus Square Identity

If x − 1/x = k, the corresponding squared value is always positive and found using x² + 1/x² = k² + 2.

Fifth Power Equivalents

If x + 1/x = k, the fifth power can be quickly evaluated using the combined product trick: x⁵ + 1/x⁵ = (x² + 1/x²)(x³ + 1/x³) − (x + 1/x).

questions.question: If one of the roots of a quadratic equation with rational coefficients is 2 + sqrt{3} , then the quadratic equation is given as ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a quadratic equation with rational coefficients, irrational roots always occur in conjugate pairs.

Given one root is 2 + √3, the second root must be 2 − √3.

Sum of roots = (2 + √3) + (2 − √3) = 4

Product of roots = (2 + √3) × (2 − √3) = 2² − (√3)² = 1

Equation is x² − (Sum)x + (Product) = 0 ⇒ x² − 4x + 1 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is x² − 4x + 1 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One root of the quadratic equation = 2 + √3

The coefficients of the quadratic equation are rational.

**Formula Used:**

Quadratic equation with roots α and β: x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0

Algebraic identity: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the roots of the quadratic equation be α and β.

⇒ α = 2 + √3

⇒ Since the coefficients are rational, irrational roots occur in conjugate pairs.

⇒ Therefore, the second root β = 2 − √3

⇒ Sum of roots (α + β) = (2 + √3) + (2 − √3)

⇒ α + β = 2 + 2 = 4

⇒ Product of roots (αβ) = (2 + √3) × (2 − √3)

⇒ αβ = (2)² − (√3)²

⇒ αβ = 4 − 3 = 1

⇒ The required quadratic equation is x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0

⇒ Substituting the values of sum and product, we get: x² − 4x + 1 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is x² − 4x + 1 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conjugate Roots Theorem

If a polynomial has rational coefficients, its irrational roots of the form a + √b always appear in conjugate pairs (a + √b and a − √b).

Complex Roots Pair

Similarly, for an equation with real coefficients, complex roots also appear in conjugate pairs of the form a + ib and a − ib.

Nature of Roots

For any general quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D = b² − 4ac. If D is not a perfect square, the roots are irrational and unequal.

questions.question: Which nitrogenous waste produced in the body is removed by the human kidney?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urea and uric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urea**, which makes up about **80% of nitrogenous waste**, is the most important one.
 
• **Urea** is produced in the** liver** and eliminated in the urine by the kidneys together with other forms of protein waste products.
 
• The breakdown of proteins in the body produces two types of waste products: **nitrogenous and non-nitrogenous**.
 
• **Carbon dioxide** and** water** are examples of non-nitrogenous waste products. 
 
• **Nitrogenous waste** products are only related to proteins because nitrogen is only found in proteins.
 
• **Urea, uric acid,** creatinine, and hippuric acid are **nitrogenous waste products**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every organism produces** waste** within the body. These wastes must be eliminated from the body.
 
• They would poison the organism if they were not expelled.
 
• **Excretion** is the process of eliminating **metabolic waste** from the body.
 
• The** excretory system** in humans consists of **two kidneys, one pair of ureters, a urinary bladder, and a urethra**.

questions.question: In Mendel’s cross, a pure tall plant (TT) is crossed with a dwarf plant (t t). The Phenotypic ratio in F2 generation is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3:1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor John Mendel** did experiments on **pea grains** to find out what the **laws of genetics** are.
 
• **Mendel** used a symbol to describe the factors involved in the inheritance of characteristics.
 
• He chose **seven pairs** of properties of peas, each of which had the ability to suppress another property during the experiment.
 
• For example, **"T" for tallness** and **"t" for dwarfism** are represented as capital letters in English letters.
 
• The crossing of two plants based on a single trait is called a **monohybrid cross**.
 
• Mendel chose two of these subspecies of pea plants, one tall and the other short because they had opposite traits.
 
• When they were crossed, all of the plants that grew from the seeds in the** first generation** were **tall**. All of these **F1** plants are the first generation of plants. 
 
• Then, he **self-pollinated** the plants obtained from the **F1** generation and discovered that the ratio of tall to short plants in the **F2 generation** was **3:1**. This ratio is also known as a **hybrid ratio**.
 
• Therefore, the **Phenotypic ratio is - 3 :1 (3 tall and 1 dwarf)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetics** is the branch of biology that studies **heredity and variation**.
 
• With his scientific discoveries, Gregor John Mendel created the foundation for **modern genetics**.
 
• As a result, he is also known as the **Father of Genetics**.

questions.question: A light ray enters from medium A to medium B, and as a result, it bends away from the normal in the medium B. The refractive index of medium B relative to medium A is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **less**__** th**an unity.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• **Refraction **is the process by which a wave bends when it encounters a medium that has a **speed **that is different from its own.
 
• The light beam is refracted as it passes through a **fast medium **and enters a **slow medium**, which causes it to bend in the direction of the boundary between the two media.
 
• The degree of **bending depends **on the **two media's indexes **of refraction.
 
• The **refractive index **determines how much a light beam **bends **when it passes through **one medium **and then **another**.
 
• When moving from medium A to medium B,**if**** medium A** is **rarer **and **medium B **is **denser **, the ray of light bends towards the normal in this circumstance.
 
• In contrast to denser media, rarer media have a greater light speed than denser media do.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Refraction in physics is the change in **direction **that results from a wave's change in **speed **as it passes through a medium.
 
• For instance, **waves **move more **quickly **in **deep water **than they do in **shallow**.
 
• When an ocean wave hits a beach at an **angle**, the wave's farther-reaching section will travel quicker than its nearer-the-beach component.
 
• The outcome is that the wave will turn until it is **traveling perpendicular **to the **coastline**.
